articles.title: College football Week 10 players to watch: Can LSU's Sam Leavitt sustain his momentum after back-to-back games without a turnover?
articles.summary: Leavitt looks to stay hot against Alabama and pick up his biggest win as a Tiger to date.
articles.body:
Christmas is just under two months away, but College Football Christmas may come in Week 10.

After the first 2026 CFP rankings on Tuesday, seven Saturday matchups now feature both teams ranked in the current Top 25. It's clear the committee is going to let this weekend solve some of the ranking scenarios, making the games that much more important and exciting.

With some marquee matchups and a full slate of other games, here are our Week 10 players to watch.

New Mexico at Nevada (Friday, 9 p.m. ET, CBSSN/DirecTV)

Brawley has four interceptions this season for the Lobos. That is tied for the sixth-most in the FBS. The safety also has back-to-back games with a pick.

Nevada quarterbacks have thrown 12 interceptions already this season. The Wolf Pack have featured four different QBs under center this year, but with those numbers it doesn't matter who they trot out. Brawley should have a good chance to come down with another INT this weekend.

No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC, DirecTV)

Leavitt was one of the biggest transfer portal names to watch last offseason, and that only got bigger when he landed at LSU under new head coach Lane Kiffin.

It looked like a perfect match in LSU's first game with a blowout win over the Clemson Tigers. The following week, he continued his hot start, throwing for 340 yards and rushing for three touchdowns. Leavitt threw three interceptions in that game against Louisiana Tech, though, and his ball security came into question.

Leavitt had varying performances over his next few games, but one constant: He threw one interception in each game.

The LSU quarterback has improved significantly over his last two games. Leavitt has completed 76% of his passes for 682 yards and seven touchdowns with no interceptions or fumbles lost in that span.

On Saturday, he will face Alabama's defense, which forces 1.5 interceptions per game, tied for the fifth-best rate in the FBS.

West Virginia at No. 15 Texas Tech (9:30 p.m. ET, ESPN/DirecTV)

Hawkins is listed as a quarterback, but he is having one of the better rushing seasons in the FBS. He has scored on the ground at least once in each game this season and has 16 rushing touchdowns, the second-most in the FBS.

His 836 rushing yards rank 15th in the FBS, and third-most for a quarterback behind Navy's Jackson Gutierrez and Army's Cale Hellums. The biggest difference is that Navy and Army both run a triple-option offense that needs a mobile quarterback to succeed. West Virginia doesn't run that type of offense, making Hawkins' performance this year so far even more impressive.

Rice at North Texas (4 p.m. ET, ESPNU/DirecTV)

White was on our list last week, and he went off for 193 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Florida Atlantic. So, keep watching him.

The North Texas running back has scored at least one touchdown in every game so far this season. He has also rushed for at least 105 yards in five straight games and at least 174 yards in back-to-back contests.

Air Force at Army (7:30 p.m. ET, CBS/DirecTV)

The battle of the triple options goes down on Saturday. Hellums' game is on the ground, and he is one of the best at using his legs. He leads the nation with 17 rushing touchdowns and is just two games removed from dropping 195 yards and five touchdowns on the ground against Florida Atlantic.

This is actually a tougher matchup on paper for Hellums. Air Force's defense allows 129.1 rushing yards per game, the 50th fewest among 138 FBS teams.

No. 7 Texas at No. 18 Missouri (Noon ET, ESPN/DirecTV)

Rodriguez has been all over the place for the Tigers' defense this season. He has 86 total tackles, the second-most in the FBS. The linebacker averages 10.75 tackles per game and has had at least nine in seven consecutive games.

The Missouri linebacker has also forced a fumble in back-to-back games. Rodriguez will lead the Tigers' defense against Texas quarterback Arch Manning.

No. 23 Oregon at No. 12 Ohio State (3:30 p.m. ET, CBS/DirecTV)

The Buckeyes played their first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin last weekend and lost 30-18 to then-unranked USC.

With no Sayin, Ohio State turned to freshman quarterback Luke Fahey under center. He played fine, completing 21 passes for 260 yards and a touchdown. Fahey didn't turn the ball over, but the offense lacked the pop it had all season with Sayin.

Fahey will get another test, as head coach Ryan Day has already named him the starter for this weekend's home game against No. 23 Oregon.

It will be interesting to see how much leash he has, or whether Day will switch to sophomore QB Tavien St. Clair, whom many expected to be the first option when Sayin went down.

articles.title: Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Playoff stakes are high in this emerging SEC rivalry
articles.summary: It's not a loser go home game, but the winner will have a clearer path to the SEC title game.
articles.body:
The College Football Playoff has altered the trajectory of the sport in so many ways, and the 24-team bracket will cause even more chaos . But one immediate benefit is that the CFP creates instant blood rivalries; there's nothing quite like the prospect of ending another team's season to fire up the blood.

Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) and Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC), which meet this weekend in a crucial SEC game, last lined up against one another on the first day of 2026 in the Sugar Bowl, and what resulted was an absolutely spectacular, 14-score game that was in doubt until literally the final seconds of the game. Ole Miss won, 39-34, but only after Georgia had tied the game with 56 seconds remaining.

The stakes when these two teams meet on Saturday in Oxford aren't quite so existential, but close. Georgia, ranked No. 2 in the initial CFP rankings, should be fine to make the playoff even with a loss, but Ole Miss, at No. 10, could be in trouble. Whoever wins gets an easier path to the SEC championship and its coveted first-round bye.

At this point in the season, everyone knows what's what, and it's just a matter of executing. And for both teams, it's a matter of containment — for Ole Miss, containing Georgia's run game; for Georgia, containing Ole Miss' do-everything quarterback Trinidad Chambliss.

Kirby Smart, in the midst of his usual glossing of the next week's opponent, lasered in on what makes Chambliss so difficult to defend against. "It's not the 'wow!' plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves," he told assembled media earlier this week. "It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. … He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways."

Chambliss, to Smart's mind, presents a unique challenge because of his talent, his experience, and his system under head coach Pete Golding. "There's nothing we're going to do that he hasn't seen," Smart said. "You're not tricking the guy. I think that's what people get infatuated with, is, 'How can I trick him and do that?' You can't do that. … There's not a perfect remedy. If there was, somebody would have done it."

The Rebels are averaging 282.1 yards through the air this season, second only to LSU in the SEC. Georgia's defense ranks sixth in the conference, giving up 186.6 yards through the air per game.

But pure yardage doesn't tell the full story; Chambliss is lethal in the red zone, making plays that give even Smart pause — "not against the Sisters of the Poor, he's doing that against SEC teams. That makes him hard to defend in the red area."

On the plus side for the Georgia defense, the Bulldogs are swarming quarterbacks at a fearsome rate — 26 sacks to date, the program's best since the landmark defensive year of 2021. However, thanks to a durable offensive line and Chambliss' legs and decision-making, Ole Miss has only given up five sacks all season. You want a focal point for this game, Georgia's ability to get to the quarterback is it.

Ole Miss, meanwhile, is willing to take its chances with Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton's arm as long as it means corralling the Georgia run game. "If you can't stop the run versus those guys, it's a long night," Golding said earlier this week. "We got to play really physical up front, be really sound at the second level and have erasers, and you can't give up explosives versus these guys."

Georgia is gaining 200.1 yards per game on the ground, third in the SEC. At the same time, Ole Miss is giving up 148.9 rushing yards per game; only Vanderbilt, Arkansas and Auburn are giving up more.

This budding rivalry is a prime case of playing through the whistle. Ole Miss held a nine-point fourth-quarter lead against Georgia last year in the regular season and lost by eight. Georgia held a nine-point halftime lead against Ole Miss in the Sugar Bowl and gave up a 22-3 run en route to losing by five.

This game is significant enough that it bumped the usual Saturday night matchup of Alabama-LSU to the afternoon. Every SEC program already has an armload of rivals, but games like this, coming on the heels of two momentum-swing brawls last year, might just create another one.

articles.title: Derby 3-1 Bolton: Rams hit back to claim a vital win and ease pressure on John Eustace
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Derby County and Bolton Wanderers at Pride Park on Friday night; Rams hit back in second half with goals from Ryan Nyambe, Jack Robinson and Rhian Brewster.
articles.body:
It was just a second win all season, a first home win at Pride Park, and a first victory in 11 games on Friday night.

They still find themselves four points adrift of safety, but will be feeling far better heading into the international break.

It looked like it was going to be another bad night for Derby as Bolton dominated the first half and took the lead just before the break through Ruben Rodrigues.

But the change was rapid after the break. Ryan Nyambe poked in his first ever career goal - in his 309th appearance - within 60 seconds of the restart. Jack Robinson then quickly netted to complete the turnaround.

Bolton pushed to find a way back, but Rhian Brewster thumped in a late third to seal a badly-needed win.

46: GOAL! WHAT A START TO THE SECOND HALF FOR DERBY! Just what they needed. They launch forward and Morris' cross from the left is flicked on by Fuseini. And Nyambe is there to poke in at the far post.

49: GOAL!! HOLD THE BACK PAGE! This league makes no sense sometimes. Derby have turned this game around! A ball into the box is headed on by Morris, and Robinson is there to finish from close range.

53: WHAT A SAVE! Morris puts a ball across for Fuseini, who turns inside and shoots, but Bonham makes a brilliant stop! He may have kept Bolton in this.

70: WHAT A SAVE! How has he kept this out?! Gale teases a cross up to Dalby in the middle. He nods it on target and Zetterstrom gets down to make a brilliant save with his forearm.

90+4: GOAL! BREWSTER BRINGS THE HOUSE DOWN! He nicks the ball off Larrazabal, and then drives into the box and buries a shot into the top corner. That's the win for Derby.

"We changed the shape at half-time, and the response from the lads was outstanding. The chips were down, we're not going great in the league, and the character of the group showed.

"It's really important that we don't get carried away with this win, but we need to enjoy it."

"We just didn't concentrate for a five-minute period after half-time. We were comfortable for the first 45 minutes, but we've got to kill teams off when we're on top.

"We should have been more than one ahead at half-time. We had big chances, big moments.

articles.title: Fermín: "Nunca me veía importante, no tenía una progresión como los demás"
articles.standfirst: "El K.O. ante el Inter y el del Atlético fueron los momentos más duros en el Barcelona", dice en una entrevista en 'Mundo Deportivo'
articles.summary: "El K.O. ante el Inter y el del Atlético fueron los momentos más duros en el Barcelona", dice en una entrevista en 'Mundo Deportivo'
articles.body: Fermín López habla del pasado y del presente en una entrevista en 'Mundo Deportivo'. El jugador del Barcelona recuerda que lo pasó mal en algunos momentos de su carrera, sobre todo durante su etapa de formación, cuando no se sentía con peso en el equipo y no veía claro su futuro. "Siempre he tenido dudas, porque nunca lo he tenido fácil, nunca me veía importante, no tenía una progresión como los demás compañeros y al final pues obviamente eso te hace pensar que tu camino aquí no seguirá hacia adelante", asegura en el diario catalán. Fermín reflexiona sobre cómo fueron esos momentos duros y cómo, en cierto modo, también le ayudaron a prepararse para el porvenir. "No jugaba, estaba lejos de la familia, pero ahora, pensándolo muchos años después y siendo mayor, lo veo como un aprendizaje y creo que me ha servido para llegar donde estoy y ser la persona que soy", dice. El jugador del Barcelona también se enfoca en el presente y lo más inmediato para los culés es el encuentro de LaLiga frente al Atlético este domingo a las 21.00 horas. Un partido en el que está en juego el liderato contra un rival que el curso anterior fue un dolor de cabeza para los azulgranas. Los de Simeone les eliminaron de la Copa del Rey y de la Champions League. "La temporada pasada nos hicieron daño, nos eliminaron dos veces. Sabemos que es un gran equipo, que nos lo va a poner muy difícil [...] El año pasado nos cogieron un poquito la medida y nos hicieron bastante daño [...] El K.O. ante el Inter y el del Atlético fueron los momentos más duros en el Barcelona", comenta en Mundo Deportivo.

articles.title: SEC reportedly discussing luxury tax on schools that spend more than the House settlement-mandated spending cap
articles.summary: Could a luxury tax dissuade schools from spending more and also provide transparency to other teams in the conference?
articles.body:
Could the SEC start collecting from schools who exceed the roster spending limits set by the House v. NCAA settlement ?

According to ESPN, the conference has floated the idea of a luxury tax among its members and "would like" to approve it by early December.

Sources told ESPN that there's still much debate on the issue, but one formula being considered would be to gradually tax schools once they exceed the annual revenue-sharing cap, which was $21.3 million for the 2026-2027 academic year. The cap will increase to about $22.2 million in 2027-28 under the terms of the House settlement. For instance, a school could be taxed 1% for the $1 million it spends over the cap and 3% for $3 million. As it escalates, there's still uncertainty. There's still work on refining the formula, as sources caution that discussions over specifics are still ongoing. The concept has been well received, but the details still need to be pinned down.

Figuring out just how much schools are spending on their rosters via revenue-sharing and NIL payments is an ever-moving target. According to The Athletic's surveys , 11 of the top-20 spending college football programs are in the SEC and the conference's average spend per team is roughly $35 million when accounting for revenue sharing payments, booster donations and other player income associated with a program.

If the SEC instituted a 1% per $1 million rule, is an extra $4 million in luxury tax revenue enough to dissuade a team from spending $20 million more than the settlement limit on its rosters? Perhaps. But it's also possible to see that added figure as the cost of doing business, especially if a premium player at a position of need becomes available in the transfer portal in football or basketball.

The conference is also reportedly undecided on what it would do with any luxury tax revenue it would receive.

The Big Ten recently enacted a $49 million NIL cap for all of its member schools. The cap would apply to a school's entire athletic department and not to individual programs.

The Protect College Sports Act has been designed to help legislate spending across the entirety of college sports, but it is becoming less and less likely that the legislation will become law. Though the PCSA has passed the Senate, it still needs to pass the House and it does not appear to be on the docket in the upcoming lame duck session with Democrats set to take control of both the House and Senate in January.

articles.title: Everton 3-1 Coventry: Thierno Barry gets two goals and an assist in comeback win as Coventry see three VAR incidents go against them
articles.summary: Report and free highlights as Everton beat Coventry 3-1; Frank Lampard's side had two penalties waved away by VAR either side of half-time, including one for a James Tarkowski hair pull; Yann Gboho put Coventry ahead, but Thierno Barry scored two and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall made it 3-1
articles.body:
Everton's only available striker scored his ninth and 10th goals of the season in similar fashion - nodding in two headers at the back post after Yann Gboho had given Coventry the lead at the start of an epic second half.

But that was only one part of the story, as officiating controversy dominated the game. In the first half, James Tarkowski avoided punishment for an apparent hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi in the penalty box.

VAR Tim Wood checked and cleared Tarkowski's challenge on the Coventry midfielder - and the technology was needed again after half-time.

Taiwo Awoniyi ran through towards the box and went down under Vitalii Mykolenko's challenge. VAR checked the foul and deemed there was contact - but outside the penalty area.

These two big calls initially didn't matter as Gboho scored his first Coventry goal in fine fashion, slaloming through challenges and poking past Jordan Pickford.

But four minutes later, Barry took over. First, he headed at the back post from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's cross before a second, similar goal had more controversy attached.

Barry bundled the winner home amid accusations from Coventry he used his hand in the move. VAR said there was no conclusive angle which showed the Everton forward handled the ball in. VAR Wood said: "Okay, that's [hit] his side, that's definitely not hand. Confirming on-field decision of goal."

Barry then turned provider to seal the result - as his eye-of-the-needle pass released Dewsbury-Hall to fire in from a tight angle. The Everton midfielder responding well to Thomas Tuchel leaving him out of the England squad earlier on Friday.

Coventry remain two points above the relegation zone and could fall into the bottom three come the end of the weekend. Everton have jumped into fifth - leapfrogging rivals Liverpool for 48 hours at least.

Lampard: VAR didn't do its job, it went against us today

Coventry head coach Frank Lampard to Sky Sports:

"The first-half decision on Tarkowski got checked. And seeing it back, he pulls on Caleb's hair while competing with Ethan [Pinnock].

"I thought the rules were clear. I know they've changed the rules so it's no red card, I get that too. But he's pulling on his hair and [Yirenkyi] can't get his momentum to jump, I think it's a foul and a penalty and they decided no.

"I thought the one on Taiwo running through - it's a clear foul that the referee doesn't give in-game. I can't believe that because it's clear. Maybe he waited for VAR because it was on the borderline.

"But as I see it, Taiwo's foot is entering the box and his knee and the back of his knee is on the line of the box, which is a penalty. That goes against us with VAR.

"And then Barry's second goal comes off his hand. I hate to sound like a moaner. It's a football match and if you win the game, that can happen here. I've worked here and know the momentum swings in the game. And I'm not trying to talk about the circumstances of the actual football.

"But when big decisions change games, they absolutely do. It's disappointing. VAR is there for that and it didn't do its job."

On Barry's second goal: "His last touch flicks it in the net. It was a really quick check a well. People may disagree, but it's my opinion."

There was no communication from the Premier League Match Centre on if the hair pull was reviewed in this game, but there was new guidance from the Premier League this summer, which reads: "A red card will be issued when there is a clear and deliberate action to pull an opponent's hair with excessive force and/or brutality.

"A yellow card will be issued if the action is deemed to be without excessive force and/or brutality.

"Referees will enhance recognition of clear holding actions that have a clear material impact, and/or non-footballing holding actions with no place on the football pitch. This includes penalising defenders where they are clearly only focused on opponents and making a holding action that is impactful on the attacker's ability to play or challenge for the ball."

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Friday Night Football:

"Sometimes you need things to go your way. You need a little bit of luck and there's no doubt they had that today.

"The Yirenkyi one should have been a penalty, the Awoniyi one should have been a penalty - the VAR brushed that aside too quickly as his foot is definitely on the line.

"That could have changed the complexity of the game. But it didn't. And Everton got the points.

"We've looked at [the second Barry goal] forensically and I do think it touches his hand. But when you're asking VAR to intervene and disallow the goal, it's difficult.

"I watched it for maybe five to ten minutes and I've come to the conclusion that I think it was, but I understand why VAR didn't give it because it's not clear and obvious enough

"It brushes his fingers. It's accidental as well, does it mean to hit his hands?

"It does divert it a little bit, but if we're going to get to that point where we're forensically looking at every single thing, it becomes hard. The frustration Frank Lampard will have is inevitable."

Moyes: I'm bothered by Coventry calls because I want result to be right!

"The efforts were good. The performance I didn't think reached the heights we did recently. But getting three points in the Premier League, you take it every way you can. It keeps us near the top end, not the bottom end.

"We had a quick turnaround from Monday to Friday. It's enough days but maybe a bit quick. We didn't perform. But I have to give Coventry credit, they did a lot of good things. You have no divine right to come here and think you're going to beat Coventry. They had opportunities and things could have gone other ways tonight.

"[The Coventry goal] was [the kick up the backside we needed]. We were just playing through and thinking we would eventually get the goal. Thierno gets another couple of goals, Kiernan got another one. It's not a night to be negative about the players, I just know we can play much better than we did tonight.

"I'm bothered because we want it [the result] to be right. But we've had a few decisions recently where we don't think have gone our way. There was one possibly at Newcastle but there was one at Man City last season in a league game which was hugely important for us regarding getting into Europe. That didn't go in our favour. Some times they go for you, something they don't. If they were going against me, I'd be complaining a bit more."

articles.title: Federal Appeals Court Hands NCAA a Victory in Struggle for Five-Year Eligibility Rule
articles.summary: DENVER (AP) — Federal appeals court judges handed the NCAA a significant victory in its struggle to implement a new five-year eligibility ruling Friday, though the win does nothing to tamp down dozens of similar lawsuits playing out in state courts across the country.
articles.body:
DENVER (AP) — Federal appeals court judges handed the NCAA a significant victory in its struggle to implement a new five-year eligibility ruling Friday, though the win does nothing to tamp down dozens of similar lawsuits playing out in state courts across the country.

Ruling in the case Wisne vs. NCAA, the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver reversed a lower-court decision that had granted players across the country who graduated high school in 2022 a fifth year of eligibility.

The lower-court ruling in July went against the NCAA's new rule that granted five years of eligibility, but only starting with athletes from the next year's class. It essentially made all those Class of '22 players eligible, leading to nationwide chaos, with teams looking to sign players who had been relegated to the sideline.

But in August, when this same appeals court first put the ruling on hold, many of those players still found their way onto rosters thanks to favorable rulings in state courts.

The decision Friday doesn't resolve some 200 state cases that involve as many as 850 athletes. The NCAA applauded it nonetheless, with chief legal officer Scott Bearby calling it "consistent with the approach taken by every federal court of appeals" in cases like these.

"The decision also acknowledges the NCAA's concern that retroactively changing eligibility rules can destabilize rosters and disrupt the settled expectations of student-athletes regarding roster spots and playing time," Bearby wrote in a memo to NCAA members.

Much of that damage has already been done, as football's regular season heads into its final month with some players — for instance, Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos — toggling on and off rosters depending on the latest court ruling. Basketball season started this week under similar uncertainty.

The decision hinged over what judges said was the plaintiffs' inability to define the market for players — a key point in determining how those players are being harmed by being declared ineligible.

In the decision penned by Judge Carolyn McHugh, the three-judge panel knocked down the plaintiff argument that all Division I players, regardless of sport, formed a single market.

"Obviously, a football player looking for a Division I roster spot would not view the 101 schools without a football program as reasonably good substitutes," McHugh wrote.

articles.title: Sivera frena al Sevilla
articles.standfirst: El meta babazorro sostuvo a su equipo y le paró un penalti a Vargas en la primera mitad
articles.summary: El meta babazorro sostuvo a su equipo y le paró un penalti a Vargas en la primera mitad
articles.body: Con la herida abierta y el recuerdo vivo en el primer homenaje de la jornada 12 a Jesús de Miguel, futbolista del Tenerife tristemente fallecido el pasado martes, Sevilla y Alavés midieron fuerzas en un Sánchez-Pizjuán que también conoce el dolor de una pérdida. Con un nudo en la garganta y tras el solemne minuto de silencio con los jugadores de ambos equipos abrazados en el césped, tocaba hablar de fútbol. El Alavés respira aunque suma una nueva jornada sin ganar, y van ocho, y el empate le sabe a poco al Sevilla por las ocasiones que tuvo. Ambos conjuntos querían recuperar sensaciones tras los últimos tropiezos antes de llegar al parón de selecciones. En un partido muy ajustado, con más arreones que fútbol, la calidad marca la diferencia y, si no la hay, y además fallas un penalti, pasa lo que pasa. Empezó con más energía el conjunto vitoriano y en una jugada rápida, Ángel centró al segundo palo y Youssef, totalmente solo, estrelló el remate de cabeza en el lateral de la red. Primer susto de la noche. El partido avanzaba a trompicones, el Sevilla se volcaba por la banda izquierda y al cuadro albiazul le costaba conectar en el último tramo. Iba a costar abrir el marcador. Al final, no lo hizo. Isaac pidió penalti en su pugna con Tenaglia, pero no hubo nada. Sí se lo señalaron a Vargas, pero Sivera evitó el primero del Sevilla. Félix Correia se iba al suelo en una acción con Ángel Pérez y, aunque dudoso, Luis Bestard pitó la pena máxima. El suizo le pegó a la derecha del meta albiazul, que aguantó y adivinó el lanzamiento para despejar hacia la banda. No fue el mejor disparo para recuperar la confianza... Antes de eso, un córner cerrado de Youssef obligó a Odysseas a meter los puños y Blanco truncó una ruleta de Vargas en la frontal. El extremo sacó una buena falta para el Sevilla, Suazo se pidió el balón y su disparo superó la barrera, pero el balón no bajó a tiempo. Parece que el penalti fallado animó a los andaluces y un disparo de Vargas provocó una buena estirada de Sivera. Tendrá pesadillas el suizo con el meta babazorro. Todavía quedaría tiempo para la anécdota. El árbitro pitó el final en el minuto 48 y se dio cuenta que se había equivocado porque señaló cuatro de añadido. Disimuló, o lo intentó, señalándose el pinganillo y reanudó el juego. En ese momento era el Sevilla quien controlaba el esférico. Pitada al canto. Juan Iglesias se vistió de delantero en la segunda parte con un par de ocasiones claras. Suazo puso el centro, cabezazo picado del '2' en boca de gol y Sivera despejó sacando una buena mano arriba. Lo volvería a intentar más adelante y Pablo Ibáñez sacó el balón sobre la línea. Había perdido solidez el centro del campo del Alavés y Quique movió el banquillo para renovar la sala de máquinas. Félix puso la quinta y su disparo con rosca al palo largo se marchó fuera por muy poco. Le faltaba calidad al Sevilla para rematar un partido que volvía a igualarse. La imprecisión en la defensa de una jugada a punto estuvo de darle el primero al conjunto vitoriano. Remate de cabeza de Boyé, toque de Valentini y casi marcó Protesoni. Llegadas sin finura mientras se acumulaba el cansancio y los nervios. Pesaba el miedo a perder al menos un punto. Llega el parón. Toca resetear.

articles.title: JJ Gabriel, con MARCA: "Mi sueño es ganar el Balón de Oro"
articles.standfirst: MARCA da en exclusiva en Madrid con la joya inglesa de 16 años, que ya se entrena en la capital mientras el club blanco ultima su fichaje para el Castilla
articles.summary: MARCA da en exclusiva en Madrid con la joya inglesa de 16 años, que ya se entrena en la capital mientras el club blanco ultima su fichaje para el Castilla
articles.body: Es viernes y anochece pronto en Madrid, como en cualquier tarde otoñal. JJ Gabriel (Reino Unido, 2010) acaba de entrenar y camina sin prisa cuando este periódico le entrega la primera portada que protagoniza, la misma que anuncia su flamante fichaje por el Real Madrid. El futbolista, de dieciséis años recién cumplidos, la mira y sonríe. “¿Me la puedo quedar?”, pregunta mientras posa con ella como un niño que se acaba de hacer con su cromo favorito. Es la primera. Su primera. De una carrera que apunta a reunir unas cuantas más. Lleva días instalado en la ciudad que aspira a convertir en su casa. La recorre y, sobre todo, se entrena a doble sesión. Por la mañana sobre el césped, en solitario y bajo la batuta de un preparador personal; por la tarde en el gimnasio. Lo hace ya desvinculado del día a día del filial del Manchester United, el club al que todavía pertenece a efectos federativos. La elección no le plantea dudas. Cuando le preguntamos por qué es mejor Madrid que Barcelona, responde con su gesto facial antes que con la boca: “Obviamente, Madrid”. A su lado, su padre, Joe O’Cearuill, exfutbolista y guía deportivo de la joven perla, reafirma entre risas. Padre e hijo atienden a este diario con amabilidad. Pero JJ no solo trae compañía. Sus maletas aterrizaron en Madrid cargadas de metas. “Mi sueño es ganar un Balón de Oro”, nos desliza en su inglés natal antes de marcharse, agradecido por el obsequio, la edición de ayer de este periódico entre manos. A sus dieciséis años, JJ Gabriel trata ser lo más profesional que puede mientras persigue una meta de adultos. Tras apartarse de la rutina del United en Carrington, se ejercitó primero en Barcelona y ahora lo hace en Madrid, la ciudad en la que su representante, Ali Barat —con él desde hace poco menos de un mes—, trabaja en dos frentes: cerrar los términos del contrato con el Real Madrid y buscar acomodo para el futbolista y su familia. El primer asunto es el que marca la actualidad. El club blanco quiere incorporarlo a su filial, el Real Madrid Castilla, esa antesala por la que pasaron Vinicius o Valverde camino de la cumbre del primer equipo. No podrá disputar la Youth League (competición en la que debutó anotando un hat-trick) vestido de blanco esta temporada porque su inscripción federativa continúa ligada al United, que lo mantiene en sus registros pese a que el jugador ya no entrene con los Red Devils. Ese es el principal menester que está frenando la oficialidad del movimiento, aun con la mayoría de edad futbolística cumplida hace unas semanas. El marco normativo y las fechas explican tanta demora. El artículo 19 del Reglamento sobre el Estatuto y la Transferencia de Jugadores prohíbe, con carácter general, los traspasos internacionales de menores de 18 años, pero admite una excepción para los futbolistas de entre 16 y 18 años con nacionalidad comunitaria que se mueven dentro del ámbito europeo. La propia guía de la FIFA contempla que un jugador con pasaporte de un país de la UE pueda acogerse a esa excepción aunque proceda de una federación ajena a la Unión, de modo que el pasaporte irlandés de JJ Gabriel resulta determinante. A ello se suma el calendario: el mercado de invierno, en enero, será la primera ventana para formalizar su inscripción, por lo que no sería extraño que su anuncio se prolongue, comenta su entorno. Mientras tanto, el United estudia cómo resarcirse de una marcha que duele en Carrington dada la proyección del futbolista. Si JJ Gabriel terminase fichando por el Real Madrid, equipo extranjero para los británicos, la compensación por formación rondaría las 350.000 libras. Para retenerlo, el United llegó a ofrecerle un palco en el futuro Old Trafford y un contrato de renovación. No fue suficiente para frenar un sueño que está viviendo el prólogo.

articles.title: Northwestern's Grid Iron Grilled Cheese, Top Concession Menu Items at New Ryan Field Shown in Video
articles.summary: Northwestern's new stadium features plenty of dining options for hungry fans.
articles.body:
Northwestern's new stadium features plenty of dining options for hungry fans.

A video by Front Office Sports' Stadium Eats showed some of the best options on the menu for fans who attend games at Northwestern's New Ryan Field.

Among the featured options are an eight-inch-long mozzarella stick from Dimmi Baby and the "Grid Iron" grilled cheese from Goatdown, which includes three cheeses with caramelized onions and kimchi in sourdough bread. Goatdown also offers a cheesesteak with shaved ribeye, cheese, caramelized onions, mustard and giardiniera in an Italian baguette.

Dining options can be found in the Northwest Plaza at The Village , a culinary district which features a collection of the city's finest establishments.

There are even more options in the Southwest Plaza near the tailgating area. The offerings can vary each game, ranging from burgers to corn roasters. The stadium even offered an Oktoberfest theme with grilled brats during Northwestern's 45-15 victory over Ball State in early October.

Inside the stadium, neighborhood restaurants from Evanston or Wilmette run pop-up stands throughout the concourses. Every concession area is positioned so fans in line can still see the action on the field. Food can also be ordered through the stadium app.

Northwestern finally opened the 35,000-seat stadium after years of build up. The $875 million stadium was privately funded by the Ryan family, who are Northwestern donors. The student section holds 2,000 placeholders with aluminum bleachers instead of seats.

The Wildcats have gotten off to a hot start in New Ryan Field and currently hold a 6-2 record. They will host the Iowa Hawkeyes on Saturday.

articles.title: La roja a Espejo y el gol de Natalio tumban al Extremadura
articles.standfirst: El veterano delantero del Avilés anota el gol decisivo a sus 42 años
articles.summary: El veterano delantero del Avilés anota el gol decisivo a sus 42 años
articles.body: Lo que durante más de ochenta minutos fue un partido igualado y tenso terminó convertido en una exhibición. El Real Avilés, lejos de conformarse con el empate que había firmado el CD Extremadura en el minuto 79, respondió con una ráfaga demoledora que dejó el marcador en un contundente 5-2 en la jornada 11 del Grupo 1 de la Primera Federación. Tres goles en los últimos cinco minutos, incluido un doblete colectivo en el 90, firmaron una de las remontadas más explosivas de la temporada. FICHA TÉCNICA Real Avilés: Ratón; Iker Alday, Sillero, Carmona, Osky; Pitu Doncel (Samu Mayo, 70’), Iñigo Muñoz, Álex Neskes; Cris Montes (Natalio, 84’), Berto Cayarga (Lidueña, 70’) y Santamaría (Santi Franco, 91’). Extremadura: Robador; Ismael (Cordero, 58’), Espejo, Sergi Molina, Álex Macías; Nordin (Chus Villar, 88’), Marco Manchón (Alfred Gothler, 88’), Luis Nicolás, Diego Díaz (Iker Burgos, 68’); Escudero y Gio Zarfino (Yael, 68’). Goles: 1-0 (15’): Osky. 1-1 (30’): Diego Díaz. 2-1 (56’): Berto Cayarga. 2-2 (79’): Iker Burgos. 3-2 (85’): Natalio. 4-2 (98’): Santi Franco. 5-2 (101’): Lidueña. Árbitro: Bárcenas Torres, del colegio riojano. Amonestó a los locales Santamaría, Lidueña, Pitu Doncel y Berto Cayarga; y a los visitantes Luis Nicolás, Cordero y Diego Díaz. Roja a Espejo (54’). Campo: Municipal Román Suárez Puerta. Un primer tiempo de pulso igualado El guion no anticipaba semejante desenlace. El Avilés, dueño del balón (66% de posesión y 555 pases por los 271 del rival), golpeó primero en el minuto 15 a través de Osky Menéndez, el mejor de los suyos con una valoración de 7.8 y tres remates. Pero el Extremadura, lejos de encogerse, igualó en el 30 con un tanto de Diego Díaz, servido por Nordin Al Lal, para firmar el 1-1 con el que se llegó al descanso. La estadística de tiros confirma el dominio local: 16 remates por 10, siete a puerta por tres, y un gol esperado de 1.57 frente a 0.95. El Avilés mandaba, pero no acababa de romper la resistencia visitante. El punto de inflexión: la roja de Espejo El partido giró en el minuto 54. El central visitante Diego Espejo, tras una revisión del VAR que elevó su amonestación a expulsión, dejó al Extremadura con diez hombres. Apenas dos minutos después, el capitán Berto Cayarga aprovechó un centro de Cristian Montes para poner el 2-1 y devolver la ventaja a los locales. Con el marcador a favor y un futbolista de más, el Avilés parecía tenerlo encarrilado. Pero el fútbol guarda giros: en el minuto 79, el recién ingresado Iker Burgos —que apenas tocó cuatro balones en todo su paso por el césped— remató un servicio de Yael Ballesteros, autor de tres pases clave y la mejor nota del Extremadura (7.9), para firmar el 2-2 y silenciar las gradas. El vendaval del descuento Cuando el empate olía a definitivo, el Avilés sacó su versión más letal. En el minuto 85, Natalio Poquet, que había entrado solo un minuto antes, culminó una asistencia de Álvaro Santamaría Varo para el 3-2. Fue el preludio de una traca final irrepetible. En el minuto 90 llegaron, casi encadenados, el 4-2 de Santi Franco —otro suplente, con apenas catorce minutos en sus piernas y dos disparos entre los tres palos— y el definitivo 5-2 de Daniel Lidueña, asistido por Álex Neskes. El banquillo avilesino decidió el encuentro: Poquet, Franco y Lidueña, los tres recién llegados, firmaron tres de los cinco goles. La diferencia de acierto quedó retratada en los metadatos del partido: el meta visitante David Pinto Robador cerró con una valoración de 4.6 y un registro de goles evitados muy negativo, síntoma de una tarde en la que el Extremadura se desangró en los últimos compases. Protagonistas de un festival ofensivo Más allá de los goleadores, el partido tuvo nombres propios en el reparto. Álvaro Santamaría Varo (7.7 de valoración, una asistencia y tres pases clave) y Cristian Montes (7.1, tres pases clave y una asistencia) fueron los arquitectos del juego ofensivo local. En la medular, Álex Neskes (7.2) aportó equilibrio y el pase del quinto. En el Extremadura, pese a la derrota, destacaron Nordin Al Lal (7.1, cinco entradas y una asistencia), el capitán Giovanni Zarfino (7.1) y, sobre todo, Yael Ballesteros, cuyo impacto desde el banquillo —con dos ocasiones claras generadas— estuvo a punto de robar un punto antes del colapso defensivo. Lo que deja la clasificación El triunfo refuerza al Real Avilés en la zona noble del Grupo 1. Los asturianos escalan hasta la tercera posición con 17 puntos (5 victorias, 2 empates y 4 derrotas en 11 jornadas), empatados con Mirandés y Racing de Ferrol, y a once puntos del líder, el CD Lugo, que suma 28. Con 23 goles a favor, el Avilés se confirma como uno de los conjuntos más productivos de la categoría en ataque. Para el CD Extremadura, la derrota supone un frenazo. El conjunto azulgrana se queda sexto con 16 puntos (5 victorias, 1 empate y 5 derrotas), un balance que lo mantiene rozando los puestos de promoción pero con una fragilidad defensiva —15 goles encajados— que esta noche quedó cruelmente expuesta. Conclusión El 5-2 engaña si solo se mira el resultado. Durante la mayor parte del encuentro hubo partido, con un Extremadura valiente que incluso llegó a empatar en inferioridad numérica. Pero la pegada del banquillo avilesino y la claudicación visitante en el tramo final convirtieron una tarde ajustada en una goleada que resonará en el Grupo 1. El Avilés se reivindica como un equipo capaz de ganar por muchos caminos; el Extremadura, en cambio, deberá revisar por qué se le escapan los puntos cuando el reloj aprieta.

articles.title: Carlos Espí: 51 minutos y nueve puntos para el Madrid
articles.standfirst: Apenas juega, pero su presencia en el campo va de la mano de momentos decisivos
articles.summary: Apenas juega, pero su presencia en el campo va de la mano de momentos decisivos
articles.body: No marcó en el AEK Arena, pero su entrada al campo para jugar unos pocos minutos volvió a ir de la mano de un subidón de adrenalina para el Real Madrid. Esa es la historia de Carlos Espí en su primera temporada vestido de blanco. En esa métrica tan utilizada en baloncesto, el más/menos, los números del delantero valenciano son impresionantes. En esta estadística avanzada, que mide el impacto directo de un jugador en el marcador mientras está en la pista, y trasladada al fútbol, al Real Madrid y al caso de Carlos Espí, se traduce en nueve puntos para el equipo de Mourinho. En Atenas entró en el campo a falta de cuatro minutos para el 90, con empate a dos en el marcador. No marcó, pero entre los cuatro minutos de juego que quedaban y los cuatro de añadido llegó el zapatazo de Fede Valverde que le dio al Madrid su quinta victoria sobre la bocina en lo que va de temporada. En todas ellas aparece en escena la salida al campo de Espí a la desesperada "Los tenemos en su sitio. Ganamos el primer partido sobre la hora. Cuando sucede tantas veces, no es una casualidad", aseguraba Mourinho en la sala de prensa de Atenas. Como tampoco parece casualidad que la entrada de Espí en el campo dé resultados desde el primer momento. El Madrid de Mourinho abrió la competición con una victoria en el campo del Espanyol gracias a un gol del delantero valenciano. En Cornellà entró en el minuto 80, con 1-1 en el marcador, y a falta de segundos para el 90 marcó el tanto del triunfo. De un punto, el Madrid pasó a sumar tres. Ese esquema de victoria, el de entrar con empate y que el Madrid gane el partido tras la entrada de Espí, se ha repetido dos veces más. Una de ellas con gol suyo. En Elche entró en el 85, con 2-2 en el marcador, y en el 90 hizo el 2-3. La otra fue ante el AEK, con el mismo resultado a su entrada y el mismo desenlace. La gran remontada de las cinco del Madrid es la de Roma, cuando perdía 3-1 a falta de media hora y acabó ganando 3-4. "Daba igual perder 3-1 que 5-1", explicaba Mou en el Olímpico para justificar sus cambios tras el tercer gol de la Roma. El inicio de la remontada llegó con un gol de Espí. El Madrid pasaba de sumar cero puntos a sumar tres. Ese el día que más tiempo ha estado en el campo: 12. El delantero de Tavernes de la Valldigna, que volverá a estar con la sub 21, ha jugado en cinco partidos más. Ante Málaga, Sevilla, Real Sociedad y Leipzig, sus pocos minutos llegaron con el encuentro ya resuelto. Sólo ante el Betis, donde el Madrid perdió 1-0, no tuvo efecto la entrada de Espí. Nada más marcar el Betis a través de Troy Parrott, Mourinho quitó a Valverde y metió en el campo a Espí. Era el minuto 81. En ese poco tiempo, Espí marcó un golazo de chilena, anulado por fuera de juego, se encontró con un paradón de Álvaro Valles y Mbappé erró un penalti. El sábado, Espí regresa con el Madrid a su tierra, a Mestalla. Al Valencia se le escapó un delantero valenciano que acabó llevando sus goles al Levante. Lo hace como el jugador de la plantilla que menos minutos acumula: 51. Pero nadie presenta una efectividad comparable ni en goles, tres, a uno cada 17 minutos, ni en el más/menos: nueve puntos para el Madrid, seis goles a favor, tres de ellos suyos, y ninguno en contra.

articles.title: Quique: "Hay que dar valor al esfuerzo de los jugadores"
articles.standfirst: El técnico madrileño cuestionó la decisión arbitral en la acción del penalti
articles.summary: El técnico madrileño cuestionó la decisión arbitral en la acción del penalti
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores puso en valor el punto conseguido por su equipo en su visitan al Sánchez-Pizjuán. Análisis: "Es un partido que nos ha llevado a una intensidad y una agresividad muy alta. Hemos igualado al rival en eso y eso nos ha permitido puntuar. El Sevilla es un equipo que aprieta mucho y su afición también. En la contención hemos estado muy bien y hemos dejado la portería a cero. Es la cuarta en doce partidos. Está muy bien comparando con la temporada pasada en la que se consiguieron cinco. Hay que darle valor al esfuerzo de los jugadores". Poca producción ofensiva: "Estábamos apretados y ellos en intensidad son buenos y no dejan girar. Las veces que hemos girado hemos hecho ocasiones claras de gol, sobre todo la del primer minuto. Nos hubiese gustado llegar más de ese modo, pero no hemos tenido esa capacidad y también tiene que ver con el esfuerzo del Sevilla para recuperar rápido el balón". Regreso a Nervión: "Volver al Sánchez Pizjuán ha sido fantástico porque tengo muy buenos recuerdos y buenas sensaciones de aquella época en la que nos unimos mucho para hacer las cosas bien". Sevilla: "Hacer conciencia de la realidad es importante y cuando lo haces, desde ese asentamiento, las cosas pueden salir con otra intención. Antes había un desencuentro entre la realidad y el optimismo. Todo el mundo ha aceptado la realidad y desde ahí se empuja para que el equipo lo haga bien. Los jugadores ahora se sienten con la obligación, pero sin esa presión insana, de querer hacer lo que no tienen". Sivera: "Respeto mucho la tarea arbitral, pero creo es un penalti que no se ha debido lanzar. Es el segundo penalti que para Sivera. Paró uno en Bilbao en el mismo lado y son acciones de valor gol y que significan puntos. No ha tenido que hacer grandes intervenciones, pero en la más importante, ha estado presente".

articles.title: Everton 3-1 Coventry: Frank Lampard says VAR didn't do its job after three incidents went against Sky Blues in Premier League defeat
articles.summary: Three VAR reviews went against Coventry in their defeat to Everton; James Tarkowski's hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi was not penalised; Vitalii Mykolenko's clip on Taiwo Awoniyi also not given as a penalty; there were handball calls for Thierno Barry's second goal
articles.body:
Two penalty appeals and a possible handball for Everton's second goal were all reviewed by VAR officials Timothy Wood and Gary Beswick, but nothing was given. They were also not awarded on-field by referee Stuart Attwell.

Coventry opened the scoring after the two penalty appeals, but were ultimately beaten 3-1 on Merseyside on Friday Night Football.

Lampard told Sky Sports: "I hate to sound like a moaner. It's a football match and if you win the game, that can happen here. I've worked here and know the momentum swings in the game.

"I'm not trying to talk about the circumstances of the actual football, but when big decisions change games, they absolutely do. It's disappointing. VAR is there for that and it didn't do its job."

Here, we breaks down each incident and what the pundits, managers and players had to say...

Tarkowski avoids punishment for elbow and hair pull

Towards the end of the first half, James Tarkowski rose to defend a high ball into the box. As he did, he caught Ethan Pinnock with an elbow, before also appearing to pull the hair of Caleb Yirenkyi.

VAR did look at the incident, especially the elbow, but nothing was given in terms of a card or a penalty.

There was no communication from the Premier League Match Centre on if the hair pull was reviewed, but there was new guidance from the Premier League this summer, which says: "A red card will be issued when there is a clear and deliberate action to pull an opponent's hair with excessive force and/or brutality.

"A yellow card will be issued if the action is deemed to be without excessive force and/or brutality.

"Referees will enhance recognition of clear holding actions that have a clear material impact, and/or non-footballing holding actions with no place on the football pitch. This includes penalising defenders where they are clearly only focused on opponents and making a holding action that is impactful on the attacker's ability to play or challenge for the ball."

"The first-half decision on Tarkowski got checked. Seeing it back, he pulls on Caleb's hair while competing with Ethan.

"I thought the rules were clear. I know they've changed the rules so it's no red card, I get that too. But he's pulling on his hair and [Yirenkyi] can't get his momentum to jump. I think it's a foul and a penalty and they decided no."

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Friday Night Football: "Yirenkyi goes up, Tarkowski gets hold of his hair. He yanks it down. Is it excessive force? Probably not, but he pulls his hair, stopping any elevation. It's a definite penalty for me.

"Yirenkyi knows he has his hair pulled. It's unusual for Tarkowski to do. It's not the best piece of defending that's for sure... It's a foul. It's not a red card anymore but it's definitely a foul."

Lee Hendrie on Sky Sports co-commentary: "There's a clear pull... Tarkowski is in the heart of this. There's an elbow, which isn't a problem, but the hair pull will raise awareness.

"You can clearly see he's utilising the hair. It's a tight one. VAR have completely not looked at it or felt the need to look at it."

At the start of the second half, Taiwo Awoniyi drove into the box with Vitalii Mykolenko behind him. There was some contact from behind which sent the striker down.

Referee Stuart Attwell said no penalty, while the VAR review deemed the contact to be outside the box.

"I thought the one on Taiwo running through - it's a clear foul that the referee doesn't give in-game. I can't believe that because it's clear. Maybe he waited for VAR because it was on the borderline.

"But as I see it, Taiwo's foot is entering the box and his knee and the back of his knee is on the line of the box, which is a penalty."

"It's a definite penalty and it's rubbish from the VAR. It's a poor decision. It's a definite foul, they rush it too quickly, and his foot's on the line.

"VAR said it was outside the box - but it's on the line. If you're in the line, you're in the box.

"Awoniyi puts his right foot across and then Mykolenko just gets him. It's on the line. It's a definite foul and goes over. Mykolenko goes over as well.

"Just take a breather, tell the referee to have a look at it and he will have come to a different conclusion."

Did the ball hit Barry's hand before his second goal?

There was a question of handball before Barry's second goal which gave Everton the lead. He bundled home from Tyrique George's cross, with the ball bouncing wildly.

VAR did check the goal, but there was no conclusive evidence of handball and the goal was allowed to stand.

Friday Night Football later revealed what VAR had said about the incident. VAR official Wood said in his deliberations: "Okay, that's his side, that's definitely not hand. Confirming on-field decision of goal."

However, on Sky Sports co-commentary, Hendrie maintained he believed it was a handball and should have been ruled out.

It was a sentiment that, unsurprisingly Lampard agreed with, telling Sky Sports: "Barry's second goal comes off his hand... His last touch flicks it in the net. It was a really quick check as well. People may disagree, but it's my opinion."

When asked about it, goalscorer Barry said: "A goal is goal! I scored two goals today... It's the job of the striker to score. I'm in a good moment and I try to keep this feeling."

Redknapp: It was a handball for Barry goal - but hard for VAR

"We've looked at it forensically and I do think it touches his hand. But when you're asking VAR to intervene and disallow the goal, it's difficult.

"I watched it for maybe five to 10 minutes and I've come to the conclusion that I think it was, but I understand why VAR didn't give it because it's not clear and obvious enough.

"To me, it looks like it brushes his left hand, but we've been able to blow it up and look at it. A good game is a quick game and we don't want VAR to intervene and take 10 minutes.

"It's not as conclusive as we'd like to see for them [VAR] to intervene... "It brushes his fingers. It's accidental as well, does it mean to hit his hands?

"It does divert it a little bit, but if we're going to get to that point where we're forensically looking at every single thing, it becomes hard."

articles.title: Sivera: "Cada punto cuenta y queda uno menos para el objetivo"
articles.standfirst: El portero fue determinante con un penalti parado a Vargas
articles.summary: El portero fue determinante con un penalti parado a Vargas
articles.body: El Alavés no pudo poner fin en el Sánchez Pizjuán a su sequía de victorias, pero al menos logró puntuar y dejar la portería a cero después de los seis goles que encajó seis días atrás en el Camp Nou. Los babazorros estuvieron lejos de su mejor nivel con balón y en días así no hay nada como evitar que el rival haga gol para, al menos, poder sumar un punto. Antonio Sivera fue el gran artífice del empate babazorro. El meta de Javea detuvo una pena máxima a Rubén Vargas en la primera mitad que mantuvo a su equipo de pie. "Ha sido la jugada más definitiva de todo el partido. Esta mañana lo habíamos estudiado muy bien y gracias a Dios nos ha vuelto a salir. Hemos parado otro penalti que le permite volver a sumar al equipo". El empate no permite al Alavés cumplir el objetivo que se había marcado en su visita a Sevilla de poder irse al parón con un triunfo y ya son dos meses sin saborear una victoria. "Son muchas jornadas sin ganar, pero al final los que llevamos mucho tiempo sabemos que cada punto cuenta y es uno menos para lograr el objetivo. Hoy hemos venido a un campo difícil, donde el Sevilla estaba en una buena dinámica y hemos sabido pelear un punto que para nosotros es importante". Sivera también tuvo unas palabras de solidaridad hacia Jesús de Miguel. "Han sido días difíciles y la mejor manera de honrar su nombre era jugar, transmitir esa pasión que seguro que le habrá llegado allí arriba y mandar un abrazo a su familia porque seguro que están pasando momentos difíciles".

articles.title: Coventry City: Frank Lampard questions decisions after Sky Blues fall at Everton
articles.summary: Coventry had a trio of decisions go against them in defeat at Everton, with Frank Lampard suggesting a hair pull should have been a penalty.
articles.body:
Coventry boss Frank Lampard questioned why his side were not given a penalty after a trio of decisions went against them in defeat at Everton .

Thierno Barry's double and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's late goal helped the hosts come from behind to win 3-1 on Friday .

Yann Gboho gave Coventry the lead after the break, yet the visitors felt they should have had a first-half spot-kick.

James Tarkowski tugged Caleb Yirenkyi's hair while jumping for a ball, with referee Stuart Attwell dismissing the Sky Blues' claims.

The rules have been relaxed around hair pulling this season and it does not automatically mean a foul or a red card, with excessive force and intent also being taken into consideration - but former Everton boss Lampard believes the officials got it wrong.

He said: "They're saying it's not enough of a pull and I think it's a hard area to be in. What is a hair pull? You've decided it is but it's not enough.

"I have looked at them, sometimes with emotions in the moment you can't be clear on the sidelines.

"I think the rules are fine. It's not a red card. I kind of get that because I think in a game of football there's a lot of stuff happens that's not absolutely dramatic.

"You know they can happen but I think if the the rule remains that it's a foul so I felt it was a foul."

Lampard also felt Taiwo Awoniyi was fouled by Vitalii Mykolenko before Coventry went ahead, although replays showed it was outside the box, and Barry handled the ball before his second goal - although video assistant referee (VAR) Timothy Wood ruled it was not a handball offence.

"Taiwo for me on the line of the box is a penalty. You've got to give the foul in real time anyway, the ref did let it go, and I felt it was a penalty," Lampard added, with defeat leaving Coventry 16th in the Premier League.

"The Barry one is handball, I've heard they are saying it didn't touch his hand but I've seen an angle where he has flicked it in with the final touch. VAR is there for that.

"I can't sit here and say I know everything and they should give all three of them, if one or two of them don't go our way, but they would clearly change the game."

Everton boss David Moyes denied Barry handled the ball and also felt the hair pulling rule needs addressing.

After his team moved fifth, the Scot said: "We've had plenty [of decisions] which have gone against us. It certainly doesn't hit his hand.

"The hair pull rule has changed so it would be a booking if it was but I still think it's ridiculous that rule is in the game. I can't understand why they don't fix this completely because I don't see it as a good rule at all."

Three big VAR calls, and they all went against Coventry . Lampard must have walked under a ladder earlier today.

There is a strong argument that the Sky Blues should have been awarded a penalty for the Tarkowski hair pull

The law was relaxed at the start of this season to say not all hair pulling should be a red card, after three players were sent off last season.

The idea is that not all contact with the hair should be an offence, and it needs to be an act with excessive force for a player to be sent off.

But, for a penalty, the actions of Tarkowski only need to be a foul, not violent conduct. If accidental, it should not be a spot-kick.

Did the Wood, the VAR, concentrate too much on a possible handball by Tarkowski within the move?

It looked like there was a movement of Tarkowski's arm to pull the hair which should have led to a VAR intervention. Coventry probably should have received a penalty.

Then early in the second half came a possible penalty as Mykolenko clipped Awoniyi.

The camera positioned level with the edge of the penalty area did seem to show the contact was outside the area, and the VAR cannot intervene to award a free-kick.

It might have been a soft VAR intervention even if the potential foul was inside the box.

Perhaps most controversially was Barry's second goal, with the ball appearing to touch the striker's arm before it went into the goal.

We have seen this kind of situation a few times this season, most notably when Nottingham Forest had a goal against Tottenham disallowed.

This time, the VAR decided he did not have the necessary conclusive proof to be sure the ball touched the hand.

Yet it does seem like there is a change of direction after Barry's hand touches the ball, and that was the reason it goes into the goal. It looked like handball should have been given on video review although others might argue that ruling it out would have been too forensic.

Three decisions, and Coventry can feel aggrieved about two of them.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza: "Sivera estuvo tres años conmigo y no paró ni un penalti"
articles.summary: El técnico sevillista subrayó que sus jugadores "dicen que han sido de las mejores segundas partes de la liga"
articles.body: Luis García Plaza atendió a los medios después del empate del Sevilla ante el Deportivo Alavés en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán (0-0). "En la segunda parte merecimos ganar sobrados y en la primera tuvimos el penalti. Nos ha costado un poco al principio, pero lo digo siempre, no es fácil ser muy superior todo el partido. No hemos sido peores, simplemente igualados. Hemos sido muy merecedores de la victoria, pero esto se trata de marcar. ¿Quién es el mejor jugador del partido? Pues eso dice todo", comenzó el entrenador del conjunto nervionense. Falta de lucidez en ataque. "Si tampoco los delanteros hacen goles, falta un jugador que a lo mejor sea capaz de cambiar el partido, y nos ha faltado estar acertados en las ocasiones que hemos tenido, que tampoco hemos generado veinte. Ya se iba cayendo Félix físicamente y ha salido Alfon, se iba cayendo Rubén y ha salido Ejuke, que le queríamos fresco para ese rato, y ni Stassin ni Isaac ni Robbie han estado acertados en el gol". Penalti errado. "Los encargados son Guridi, Peque y Vargas. Sivera estuvo tres años conmigo y no me paró ni un penalti, y este año llevo dos". Sangante. "Lo he visto muy bien quitando algún balón que ha perdido. Le he quitado por la amarilla, porque ellos jugaban con dos delanteros muy poderosos. Es un equipo que en cualquier momento te gana duelos y ha estado muy bien, incluso Castrín cuando ha salido ese rato. Había que hacer dos o tres cambios en la alineación por tema físico, porque llevamos cuatro partidos en doce días. Me alegro mucho por él, porque ha estado trabajando y esperando su momento". Posición de Fofana. "Puede jugar en los dos sitios. Primero no es un doble pivote, con todo mi respeto, es un 6 y un 8, Luci sí es un mediocentro. El otro día contra Osasuna me gustó mucho en el mediocentro y cuando le pusimos por delante en Getafe estuvo bastante flojo. Hoy no ha estado tan bien, pero confiamos en él". Incomodidad. "Los jugadores dicen que han sido de las mejores segundas partes de la liga. Lo que pasa es que no marcamos. Creo que la primera parte sí hay 25 minutos que no les hemos encontrado el sitio, pero a partir del penalti creo que hemos podido marcar cuatro o cinco goles. Soy muy exigente y ambicioso, pero llevamos 18 puntos, sumando, trabajando, peleando. Tenemos que ir creciendo, creo que el equipo ha hecho méritos para ganar, es mi sensación". Laterales. "Están haciendo buena temporada los dos, cada uno en su función. Hoy Gaby ha estado a un nivel muy, muy alto". Parón internacional. "Vamos a descansar unos días, porque al jugar viernes normalmente los equipos descansan el siguiente fin de semana. Ahora se nos van creo que siete u ocho con las selecciones. Van a ser dos semanas de prederbi. Es verdad que es un poco raro, porque nos van a faltar jugadores, a ver cuándo se pueden incorporar. Nos vamos en una situación buena, sabiendo que va a haber mucha igualdad en la Liga. Lo importante es no meterte en ese grupo de abajo y estar cuanto más arriba, mejor".

articles.body: España jugará la final de la Finalissima tras ganar a Portugal (2-2 y 8-7) en una agónica tanda en la que Jesús Herrero paró sendos lanzamientos a Silvestre Ferreira y Lúcio Júnior. España y Portugal, las dos mejores selecciones de Europa con la excepción de la sancionada Rusia, demostraron por qué lo son y, sobre todo, confirmaron que se conocen a la perfección y sus técnicos, Jesús Velasco y Jorge Braz, también, no en vano Velasco debutó como seleccionador en 2024 imponiéndose a los lusos en su país. Por este motivo, el primer tiempo fue un duelo táctico, con cambios continuos, unos para lanzar faltas, los otros para defenderlas, juego de 5 con Bernardo Paçó. Argumentos que en cualquier otro encuentro hubieran hecho moverse el marcador, pero anoche no fue el caso en los primeros 20 minutos. Como en todos los partidos FIFA, el arbitraje se hizo notar. Los colegiados colombianos dejaron jugar, lo que permitió que la intensidad portuguesa evitara cualquier alegría española. No obstante Antonio Pérez vio la primera amarilla. Pero el videoarbitraje echó un cable a España al ver los árbitros el golpe de RúbenGóis sobre David Novoa, que sancionaron tras revisarlo con la expulsión. Dos minutos en superioridad, en los que España, que disfrutó dos ocasiones claras en las zapatillas de Mario Rivillos, tampoco hizo mover el electrónico. Tras el descanso, llegaron los goles. Raya adelantó a España, respondieron Rúben Teixeira y Hugo Neves y, a 55 segundos del final, Sergio González llevó el partido a los penaltis, en los que tras 16 lanzamientos, España se ganó volver a jugar la gran final como en 2022. articles.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: England 'disappointment' fuels midfielder's Everton heroics
articles.summary: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responds to his England omission by scoring a stunning goal to inspire Everton's 3-1 comeback victory over Coventry City.
articles.body:
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall let his performance do all the talking at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday night.

The Everton midfielder endured a disappointing start to his matchday preparations just hours earlier after learning that, despite his impressive performances in recent weeks, he had been overlooked by England manager Thomas Tuchel for this month's Nations League fixtures.

It was a setback for the 28-year-old, who was tipped to earn a place in Tuchel's latest squad but was ultimately left out, with Borussia Dortmund teenager Jobe Bellingham selected instead.

By the end of the night, though, Dewsbury-Hall had every reason to smile.

The midfielder was celebrating alongside the Everton faithful after his thunderous strike helped the Blues to a comeback victory over Coventry City , securing an impressive 3-1 win and lifting them to fifth in the Premier League table.

"It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie. It's a massive dream of mine to play for my country. I know I was close," Dewsbury-Hall told Sky Sports after Everton made it back-to-back Premier League wins.

"[I'm] sad, yeah, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up."

The wait until the next international break in March will undoubtedly feel like an eternity for Dewsbury-Hall.

But the Everton midfielder is no stranger to taking the long road to success, having experienced plenty of setbacks and detours throughout his career.

He did not make his Premier League debut for boyhood club Leicester City until the age of 22, having spent previous seasons gaining valuable experience out on loan in the English Football League with Luton Town and Blackpool.

Even when his opportunity to establish himself in the Foxes' first team finally arrived, it came during a turbulent period for the club, which ultimately ended in relegation from the Premier League at the end of the following season.

After playing a starring role in Leicester's Championship-winning campaign under Enzo Maresca, the midfielder soon followed the Italian to Stamford Bridge in a deal worth £30m.

However, Dewsbury-Hall struggled for regular game time during his only season at Chelsea , featuring mainly in cup competitions with limited opportunities in the Premier League.

It was only after his move to Everton last summer, at the age of 26, that he appeared to have finally found the right environment to reignite his career and showcase the qualities that made him once such a highly regarded attacking midfielder.

Since the start of last season, Dewsbury-Hall has scored 11 goals for Everton in the Premier League and provided seven assists.

"I'm really, really enjoying it," said Dewsbury-Hall. "I've got a really good hybrid role in this team, where the gaffer is giving me the freedom to pop up all over the pitch."

Tuchel said on Friday afternoon that Dewsbury-Hall had been "very close" to earning a place in his squad, having enjoyed "a very good season" with Everton so far.

"I've got the mentality," added Dewsbury-Hall. "I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens."

Barry draws inspiration from TikTok and Haaland

It was not just Dewsbury-Hall who caught the eye against Coventry , with Thierno Barry scoring twice in the space of five minutes at the start of the second half to help Everton come from behind.

By taking his tally for the season into double figures across all competitions, the 24-year-old - who struggled for both form and confidence after joining the Blues from Spanish side Villarreal last summer - has already surpassed the eight goals he scored last season.

In fact, only Erling Haaland, with 14 goals, has scored more in all competitions than Barry's 10 this campaign for David Moyes' side.

Not only is the French forward lighting up Hill Dickinson Stadium with his goals, he is also setting the place alight with his dance moves.

Barry has made a habit of celebrating every goal with some kind of viral dance move - and that was certainly the case on Friday night.

"I was on TikTok yesterday and I saw an NFL guy do the celebration. I said to Tyrique [George] that if we scored tomorrow, we would do the dance like that, but I think he was shy to do it, so I did the dance alone," Barry told Match of the Day.

The former Basel and Villarreal frontman is also drawing inspiration from Haaland as he looks to maintain his impressive goalscoring form.

"I'm very happy because I'm a fan of him," said Barry. "I watch a lot of videos of him and try and do the things he does. If I can play with him until the end to get the Golden Boot, I will try."

Everton win caps landmark night for Moyes

Earlier in the night, Moyes equaled Harry Catterick's record for the most games as Everton manager - with 592 matches each.

The late Catterick managed the Toffees from 1961 to 1973.

"I am proud," Moyes said in Everton 's match programme.

"The thought of being the Everton manager who has managed the most games is something I'm very proud of.

" Everton has been huge for me and my family. My son David has gone everywhere and my father has lived it with us as well, watching it all.

"That's so important. What is also so important is that I'll always try to do the right thing for Everton Football Club."

articles.title: FIFA confirma sanción a Paredes por incidentes en final del Mundial y reduce la de Molina
articles.standfirst: El exjugador del Atlético de Madrid tendrá que cumplir cuatro partidos de sanción
articles.summary: El exjugador del Atlético de Madrid tendrá que cumplir cuatro partidos de sanción
articles.body: FLa FIFA aceptó parcialmente la apelación de la Asociación del Fútbol Argentino (AFA) contra las sanciones impuestas tras los incidentes en la final del Mundial 2026 que conquistó España al reducir de 7 a 4 partidos la suspensión de Nahuel Molina, pero mantuvo las 10 fechas a Leandro Paredes. La resolución también redujo la multa al defensor Molina de 90.000 a 60.000 dólares, mientras confirmó la sanción al mediocampista Paredes en 10 fechas y una multa de 90.000 dólares, según informó la AFA en un comunicado. Agregó que solicitará los fundamentos de las decisiones para recurrir ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS), al considerar que "cuenta con argumentos de hecho y derecho suficientes" para pedir la revisión. La AFA había apelado las sanciones dictadas por la Comisión Disciplinaria de la FIFA a raíz de los incidentes relativos a cantos discriminatorios registrados durante la final del Mundial, disputada en julio pasado, en la que España venció a Argentina por 1-0. La entidad argentina recibió una multa de 321.000 dólares e impuso partidos con restricción de espectadores en aplicación de distintos artículos del Código Disciplinario de la FIFA por incidentes en los partidos del equipo contra Cabo Verde, Egipto, Suiza, Inglaterra y España. También fueron sancionados entonces Thiago Almada con un partido de suspensión y el integrante del cuerpo técnico Roberto Ayala, con 3 fechas de castigo. En agosto la FIFA accedió a una petición de la AFA para que los partidos suspendidos se descuenten en amistosos y encuentros oficiales de Conmebol, "cualquiera de ellos ocurra primero".
